title: Bound and cancel provider search and detail requests end to end
description:
Fork research: parallel GPT-6 Astra source reviews, 2026-10-25. Current application baseline: 3ae404b.

## Purpose and evidence

Current handleSearch delegates to scraper v0.3.0. Endpoint.Execute constructs requests without the caller context, uses http.DefaultClient and parses an unbounded response. Existing closed #49 covers torrent/config fetches; it does not bound the scraper provider request path. Client-side cancellation of a result row therefore does not prove that provider work stops. makrron propagates request deadlines but still reads response bodies without a cap.

## Acceptance criteria

- Route provider list and /item resolution through an application-owned client carrying r.Context(), a finite overall deadline and the shared outbound policy; do not globally mutate http.DefaultClient.
- Enforce response limits on decoded/decompressed bytes before HTML/JSON parsing, bounded result counts, and bounded concurrent requests. Reject oversized/error responses clearly and distinguish failure from a successful empty result.
- Browser cancellation/disconnect and expiry must stop upstream reads/work promptly and release concurrency slots. Preserve existing immutable config replacement and provider headers.
- Use controlled HTTP servers to cover stalled headers/bodies, infinite or compressed oversized responses, cancellation, redirects, status errors, excess concurrency and successful list/item responses. Verify limits on these actual routes, not only fetchBytes.

## Scope

Implement within the existing Go engine, typed API, generated frontend models and authenticated handler chain. Use isolated legal fixtures; never test against live downloads. This is a new backlog item, not a claim that the proposed behavior already exists.
